misconceptions.believed: That f-string padding of a painted string was a normal column pad. The run count was UI.paint(...) and then padded to width 20.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Re-reading the line before running the suite, because T6's rule -- every element computes its plain-text layout first and paints last -- was in ARCHITECTURE.md two screens above what I was editing.
misconceptions.corrected_to: An escape sequence has no display width but plenty of len, so padding a painted string pads the wrong number and the column drifts the moment colour is on. Pad the plain text and paint the padded result. Verified by rendering at FORCE_COLOR=3, stripping escapes and confirming the columns match the piped output.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: The whole test suite would have passed. Every assertion in test_cli_output.py runs against escape-stripped text or a pipe, where Depth.NONE makes paint a no-op and the bug cannot exist -- so this is a defect whose only symptom is on a real terminal, in a project whose presentation rule exists precisely because that class of thing is invisible from CI. T6 landed early for this reason and M36 was the same shape. The rule is not 'strip escapes when asserting', which is already done; it is 'compute width before colour', and following it is what makes the stripped assertion meaningful.

decisions.decision: The surface renders each decision's own reason
alternatives: Generate explanation text in the view from the stored numbers
decisions.rationale: A second rendering can agree today and drift later. Exit criterion 4 says 'no hidden state', and one code path is what that means in practice.

decisions.decision: A tag with a number that is being ignored is shown, and labelled as ignored
alternatives: Show only tags that count toward a decision
decisions.rationale: 'We have a number and are ignoring it' is information. Hiding it makes the drill's choice look arbitrary and the confidence threshold invisible.

decisions.decision: limits() is generated from the content
alternatives: A written paragraph in the docs or in the view
decisions.rationale: A level gaining a tag then changes what the player is told without anyone editing prose. A caveat that has gone stale is worse than no caveat.

decisions.decision: A fourth decision source, stale, distinct from default
alternatives: Fold it into default with a longer reason
decisions.rationale: The decision is identical but the sentence is not, and telling a returning player nothing was ever measured is a lie the model can easily avoid telling.

alternatives: Prefer the codebase guess once a reading has aged out
decisions.rationale: Having actually played something, however long ago, is better evidence about the player than inferring from their code, and it is the honest thing to say.

handoff.state: T4 W1-W7 LANDED. The game measures mastery per tag, decays it, chooses a difficulty and a drill from it, and can now explain all of that including what it is not claiming. Exit criteria 1, 2, 4 and 5 verified; 3 verified for the two simulated players who can fail (Q89). 1231 tests green unpinned, 1207 pinned, verify clean on 54 reference runs.
handoff.next_action: T4 W8, deriving a function class from the Vibe Vector. This is where T4 stops being a difficulty model and starts being a character sheet, and it is the waypoint with the most ways to go wrong: criterion 6 says changing a player's scores without changing their code must never change their class, and the trajectory's last hazard says a class system is a horoscope by default unless the patterns that earned it are on screen beside it. status --why is now the obvious place for that evidence to live, so read this session's surface before building W8's.
